result.description: Chat/voice community platform; developer API lets bots and apps read/post messages, manage guilds, channels, roles, and interactions.
result.auth_detail: Bot token (Authorization: Bot <token>) from Developer Portal; OAuth2 authorization-code bearer tokens for user-delegated access; client_credentials grant (Basic client_id:secret) for bot owner token.
result.access_detail: Free: create app in Developer Portal, get bot token and OAuth2 client credentials. Some OAuth2 scopes need Discord approval; bots in 100+ guilds need verification; privileged gateway intents (e.g. message content) need approval at scale.
result.api_notes: REST v10 covers channels, messages, guilds, members, roles, webhooks, threads, interactions/application commands, users, emoji, stickers, scheduled events, etc. Real-time Gateway over WebSocket. Per-route rate limits.
result.blocker: Minor: some OAuth scopes need Discord approval; bot-centric model (bot must be invited to each guild); official MCP at docs.discord.com/mcp is docs-search only.

evidence.quote: When you create a bot user in the Developer Portal, Discord generates a **bot token**.
Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the [OAuth2 API](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/oauth2.md).
Some scopes require approval from Discord to use.
Bot users are automatically added to all apps, and are authenticated using the bot token found in your [app's settings](https://discord.com/developers/applications).
A [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) server for the Discord API using [(JDA)](https://jda.wiki/),
Verified bots](https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/23926564536471-How-Do-I-Get-My-App-Verified) do not have a maximum number of guilds.
